notes.3: Over a quarter of candidates thought that the key diagnostic feature for the identification of an insect is the possession of wings rather than the possession of three pairs of legs. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2015
notes.4: The vast majority of candidates were able to follow the key to arrive at the correct answer.
notes.6: Many candidates demonstrated careful observation and good knowledge of plant cell structure.
notes.8: Less able candidates thought that the role of the cilia lining the trachea is to trap dust particles rather than to move mucus up towards the throat.
notes.17: The link between the absorption of water by plant material and its subsequent conduction in the xylem was not known by just over a fifth of the candidates.
notes.21: About one quarter of candidates thought that plants only respired during darkness rather than continually.
notes.23: Many candidates thought that urea is made in the kidneys rather than in the liver.
notes.26: Many candidates could not distinguish between the plumule and the radicle.
notes.28: Less able candidates chose one of the options with sunlight, not appreciating that seeds usually germinate in the soil where there is no light.
notes.32: This question proved very difficult, even for the most able candidates. The vast majority did not appreciate that there were two distinct groups, each group showing smaller but essentially continuous differences between members of that group.
notes.33: The majority of candidates did not appreciate the non-cyclical nature of the energy flow.
notes.36: Over a third of candidates did not appreciate that faeces contain carbon atoms. (Such as in undigested carbohydrate found in for example cell walls, as well as other organic materials). Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2015
